solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guide's turn of phrase

indicators.note: a turn of the word phrase means its letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tour guide's characteristic way of putting things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of phrase' reads as an idiom, but 'turn of' is the anagram signal working on PHRASE; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed for leading climbers as mountain guides.

clue.text: Funny lines fed TV comedian

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters are odd or out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV comic is fed amusing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' is the anagram signal for LINES FED.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerry Seinfeld is the American stand-up who starred in his own long-running sitcom.

clue.text: Former quality spoken of mythical brand

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: spoken of signals that the word sounds like the letters entered

parts.note: calibre means quality or standard

explanation.surface: A brand of former quality now spoken of as mythical.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand is an old poetic word for a sword, so 'mythical brand' is King Arthur's sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Excalibur is the legendary sword of King Arthur, and brand is an archaic term for a sword.

clue.text: Site frequently visited — internet address that is in bar mostly

indicators.note: the address and abbreviation go inside the shortened drinking place
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a pub is a bar
a URL is a web address

explanation.surface: A favourite haunt: the web address of a bar, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the drinking place to PU; 'in' signals the insertion. The surface's 'bar' looks like a barrier, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Purlieus are one's haunts or usual surroundings, places someone frequents.

clue.text: Having sign of damage to bodywork outside, watch sound racing vehicle

indicators.note: the mark of damage sits outside, wrapped round the ticking noise

parts.note: a scar is a mark left by damage, here on a car's body
tock is the sound of a ticking watch

explanation.surface: A racing car, scraped on its bodywork, with a clock ticking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' signals the wrap; the surface makes 'watch' a verb, but it is a timepiece whose tick-tock gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is an ordinary saloon modified for rough circuit racing.

clue.text: 'Hot' trader's dealings — one might get a ticket for it

definitions.text: one might get a ticket for it

parts.note: traffic means trading or dealings
a dealer in stolen, hot, goods is a fence; the possessive is read as of fence

explanation.surface: A dealer in stolen goods does business; somebody could be fined for that.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'of', so the trader's dealings become the dealings of the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A motoring infringement such as speeding is punished with a fixed penalty notice.

clue.text: Preserve farewell vocal work

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
ta-ta is an informal goodbye

explanation.surface: Keep the goodbye song.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a choral composition with solo voices, such as those Bach wrote.

clue.text: Film star's first name ex-president won't take on

indicators.note: won't take means the word on is removed from the president's name

parts.note: Bill Clinton is a former US president

explanation.surface: A movie star's first name a former president refuses to adopt.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint Eastwood is the Hollywood star of westerns, Clint being his given name.

clue.text: In favour of broaching old rock band to get together again

indicators.note: broaching means piercing, so one piece breaks into the other

parts.note: R.E.M. was an American rock band
for means in favour of

explanation.surface: Fans back an old rock band getting back together.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-form is to form again, as a disbanded group might.

clue.text: Something to go with tea caddies, woken up rudely

indicators.note: rudely suggests a rough upheaval, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tea caddies jolted from sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' is the anagram signal for CADDIES WOKEN UP.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sponge baked with fruit at the bottom then turned over, served at teatime.

clue.text: Bring on popular dog

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Bring on the crowd-pleasing dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur trouble is to bring it upon yourself, so the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Person going to court having simple falling-out

parts.note: plain means simple or unadorned
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone suing over what was just a simple quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit before a court.

clue.text: Film director collapsed near island

parts.note: fell means collapsed or toppled
in, as in 'in the area', can mean close by

explanation.surface: A film director collapses near an island location.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was the Italian filmmaker behind La Dolce Vita and 8½.

clue.text: Less interesting flannel

definitions.meaning: comparative of flat in the sense of dull
as a verb, flannel means to sweet-talk or butter up

explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull, so the comparative is duller; flannel as a verb is insincere praise.

clue.text: Criminal began cruel hoax — it took in job-seekers

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of the following words are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook started a nasty scam, and an office fell for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' is the anagram signal for BEGAN CRUEL HOAX. A labour exchange was the old British name for a government job centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British state employment office registered the unemployed and matched them to vacancies.

clue.text: Take tiller for craft of girls' organisation

parts.note: the Guides are the girls' scouting movement
a ship is a craft

explanation.surface: Steering the boat belonging to the Girl Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the tiller means steering a vessel, i.e. directing the ship.

clue.text: A new sort of energy of the body

parts.note: atomic energy is nuclear power

explanation.surface: A new kind of bodily energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomic relates to anatomy, the structure of the body.

clue.text: Lor! boats finish in poor repair — not like this

indicators.note: being in poor repair suggests something broken up, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Goodness, the boats are finishing up in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in poor repair' is the anagram signal for LOR BOATS FINISH; boats in poor repair are the opposite of shipshape, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape and Bristol fashion means neat and orderly, the opposite of a tatty, rundown state.

clue.text: Plundering coarse material

definitions.meaning: the sack of a city is its looting

explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to loot it; hessian bags are made of rough woven cloth.

clue.text: One German article penned by agent in untidy hand

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by the agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
I is the Roman numeral one
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: An agent wrote one German article in a scrawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' signals the enclosure; the surface makes 'penned' mean written, fitting handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spidery handwriting is thin and straggling like spider legs.

clue.text: Fit rugby player has little hesitation

parts.note: a prop is a forward in rugby
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A fit rugby forward hesitates briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper and fit share the sense of suitable or appropriate.

clue.text: Polish religious symbol represents point of no return

parts.note: to rub is to polish
an icon is a holy image in Orthodox churches

explanation.surface: Polishing a sacred image is a step from which there's no going back.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar crossing the river Rubicon became the byword for an irrevocable step.

clue.text: Horns coming from zebra's skull

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Horns growing out of a zebra's skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass instruments such as trumpets and tubas are collectively called horns.

clue.text: Famous modern artist on hospital ward

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a contemporary British artist
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A famous modern artist is admitted to a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means distinguished or celebrated, a near synonym of famous.

clue.text: Frightful chap with airs — I could be hypocritical

indicators.note: frightful suggests something mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An awful man who gives himself airs admits he may be a hypocrite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful' is the anagram signal for CHAP AIRS I; 'could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees are cast in the Gospels as sanctimonious, so the adjective means self-righteous and insincere.

clue.text: Surrey town produces, among others, exuberant actor

parts.note: e.g., for example, introduces one item among others
a ham is an actor who overplays

explanation.surface: A town in Surrey stages, among others, a showy actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just southwest of London; Egham lies on the Thames near Runnymede.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in the English county of Surrey, home of Royal Holloway college.

clue.text: Gave up job and agreed a new contract

explanation.definitionFit: Quitting a post is resigning; signing on again for another contract is re-signing.

clue.text: This person's subject fails to start, having defective vision

parts.note: the setter speaking: this person's means my

indicators.note: the subject word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion

explanation.surface: My chosen subject never gets going because my eyesight is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is short-sightedness, a common defect of vision.
